name: esp2025_dispenser
story: The alarm sounds and the light flashes; the patient presses PRESS HERE and the carousel turns one step, dropping the next dose into the drawer. The drawer is pulled out and pushed back. Then the pharmacist unlocks the lid with the key, opens it to refill and locks it again.

steps.title: Open the Dynamic Simulation environment
steps.command: Environments tab > Begin panel > Dynamic Simulation
actions: Open esp2025_dispenser.iam in Inventor.
Click the Environments tab, then Dynamic Simulation.
steps.note: Dynamic Simulation works out how an assembly moves, and the forces and speeds as it moves.

steps.title: Turn constraints into joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Settings
actions: Click Simulation Settings and tick Automatically convert constraints to standard joints. Click OK.
Open Standard Joints in the browser to see the joints Inventor made from your assembly constraints.
steps.note: Parts held together with no movement between them become one rigid group, listed under Welded group.

steps.title: Check the carousel and drive joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: In Standard Joints find the Revolution joint of the carousel (its hub in the deck) and of the worm (on the motor shaft). The drive gear is in one Welded group with the carousel.
Insert Joint > 3D Contact or Worm Gear: pick the worm and the drive gear, ratio 120:1.
steps.note: A worm gear joint ties the two together: 4 turns of the worm move the carousel 12 degrees.

steps.title: Join the button, drawer, cam and lid
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Insert Joint, Prismatic: the PRESS HERE button in its hole, and the drawer in its opening.
Insert Joint, Revolution: the lock cam on the lock axis, and the lid on the hinge pin.

steps.title: The alarm and the button
steps.command: Right click the button Prismatic joint > Properties > Edit imposed motion
actions: The alarm and the light are switched by the program, not by a joint: they run from 1 s until the drop sensors see the pills (shown on the graph).
Button: 0 at 3 s, pressed 0.8 mm at 3.2 s, back at 3.4 s.
steps.note: The alarm keeps sounding until the pills have been dispensed, as the brief asks.

steps.title: Turn one dose
steps.command: Right click the worm Revolution joint > Properties > Edit imposed motion
actions: Worm: 0 at 3.4 s, 1440 degrees (4 turns) at 5 s.
The worm gear joint turns the carousel 12 degrees: the next compartment is over the drop hole.
steps.note: The self-locking worm holds the carousel still between doses.

steps.title: Take the pills
steps.command: Edit imposed motion on the drawer Prismatic joint
actions: Drawer: 0 at 6 s, 35 mm out at 7.5 s, hold to 9 s, back in by 10.5 s.

steps.title: Pharmacy refill
steps.command: Edit imposed motion on the cam and lid Revolution joints
actions: Cam: 0 at 11 s, 90 degrees (unlocked) at 12 s, hold, back to 0 (locked) by 19 s.
Lid: 0 at 12.2 s, 100 degrees open at 14 s, hold to 16 s, shut by 17.8 s. Click OK.
steps.note: Only the pharmacy key turns the cam; with the cam at 0 the lid catch cannot lift.

steps.title: Run the simulation
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player set Final Time to 20 s and Images to 1000.
Click Run. The assembly moves and the timeline fills in.
Use the slider to scrub back and forth.
steps.note: Press Play below to run the same motion here.

steps.title: Plot the results
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Results panel > Output Grapher
actions: Open the Output Grapher.
Under Standard Joints, tick the angle of the carousel and lid joints and the position of the drawer joint.
The graph shows each value against time. Click on the graph to move the simulation to that moment.

steps.title: Record a video
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player click Record (the red dot) and choose a file name and format.
Click Run again. Inventor saves a video of the motion for your portfolio.
steps.note: You can also export a moment to Stress Analysis (Export to FEA) to check a part at its highest load.
